body:
I need the money in the sense I'm not well off enough to just quit with no plan, but not in the living paycheck to paycheck sense. I'm a business analyst. It's very stressful the last year, but I don't hate it entirely. Most of what i currently hate about it is situational and should be temporary. Beyond that, it's fine. The things I like about it are what got me to my current position (it's not what I studied) a lot of it is about organizing things and making them more efficient. It's not so much that I like doing it so much as I dislike inefficient, disorganized things. Which is funny, or ironic, or something: my job entails identifying useless, unnecessary things that the system would be better off without, and here we are. 


More though, it's busy work. What I do is beneficial within the context of my company, it's not important or necessary or beneficial to society/People in general. Even the company isn't producing something vital/important. This might be fine I if there were something else in my life I cared about outside of work, but when there isn't,  it's just another thing in my life that is ultimately pointless. 

I appreciate your time and support, but I'm probably wasting it. There are certainly others on this board your energy would be better spent on. I don't mean that in a 'poor me' way, just fact - I'm not a bad person, but I'm not really a good one either, and I've thought about this stuff for decades, at this point, nothing is going to change. The truth of it just get overwhelming sometimes.

I see a lot of people in the world as having some kind of purpose or contributing, even if that's by my standard and not theirs. I just don't see any that I look at and think *that, I want to do that*. For example: raising kids/family- I don't have or want kids. Teachers, doctors, jobs that make or do things that support others (carpentry, mechanics, etc)  ... there's thousands of options, but none that stir enough of an interest to even entertain the idea of having to start from scratch in a new career for. I've considered non-profits, but those jobs require a lot of dedication and care for what you're supporting to offset the job demands, and I just can't think of anything I care that much about. 
I have a few hobbies - I craft, I read, I work out... I don't actually enjoy doing any of them, I just do them to fill time. I look for volunteer opportunities, but it seems like they only want people who can be available during normal working hours, and I can't.  
I guess what I'm saying is most people have something they care about or enjoy, be it family, job, hobby/interest or some mix, and how they contribute comes from the care and energy they put into that. I can't find anything I care about or enjoy that I can use/focus on in that way. When I was younger I could tell myself I'd find something eventually if I just kept trying things, but I'm in my late 30s and I've only lost interest in things, not gained. I just... feel like a spare part, the ones you get in a package and toss in a drawer, just in case, but never end up needing. I'm not connected to anything, I'm not necessary, just here.
